items.stem: In an IRAC-structured essay answer, what most distinguishes a high-scoring answer from a low-scoring one?

options.rationale: Length and verbatim rules alone do not earn application points.

options.text: Thorough application of law to the specific facts
options.rationale: Correct: graders reward applying the rule to the particular facts, not merely reciting rules.
Decorative terminology does not substitute for analysis.
Strong answers engage counter-arguments rather than avoid them.

items.explanation: Correct: graders reward applying the rule to the particular facts, not merely reciting rules.

items.stem: A performance task provides a file and a library. What is the best strategy for using them?

options.text: Ignore the library and rely on memorised law
options.rationale: Performance tasks test using the provided materials, not outside memorised law.

options.text: Use the provided library rules applied to the file facts to complete the assigned task
options.rationale: Correct: performance tasks are closed-universe; use the given library and file to perform the lawyering task.

options.text: Answer in bullet points with no analysis

options.rationale: A personal opinion ignores the assigned legal task.

items.explanation: Correct: performance tasks are closed-universe; use the given library and file to perform the lawyering task.

items.stem: Which TWO time-management practices help in the written components?

options.text: Allocating a fixed time budget per task before starting
options.rationale: Correct: budgeting time per task prevents overruns.

options.text: Spending a short set period outlining before writing
options.rationale: Correct: a brief outline organises the answer and saves writing time.

options.text: Writing everything known regardless of relevance
options.rationale: Irrelevant content wastes time and earns no points.
Ignoring the question asked misdirects the whole answer.

items.explanation: Correct: budgeting time per task prevents overruns.
